title: Restore WebSocket TCP_NODELAY delegation after stream ownership moved
summary: Trace the public wrapper through the protocol ownership boundary, reject a suite-green wrong-surface patch, and delegate TCP_NODELAY to the active stream.

symptoms: WebSocketHandler.set_nodelay no longer reaches the active network stream after stream ownership moves behind the protocol object.
A plausible proxy repair can pass the existing suite while changing the wrong client-side API surface.
The focused public caller contract fails even though legacy tests can remain green.
error_signatures: AssertionError on the obsolete handler stream

applies_when: A public wrapper delegates a control to a resource whose ownership moved behind another abstraction.
The issue names a public entry point whose full delegation chain can be tested.
A focused contract test can assert the call on the currently active resource.
exclusions: Do not reuse when the wrapper intentionally owns an independent stream.
Do not accept a green suite without a focused assertion beginning at the public caller named in the issue.
Do not treat this collection run as causal evidence that AEG retrieval improves repairs.

environment_fingerprint.runtime: CPython 3.8.20 used in place of unavailable CPython 3.7
dependencies: temporary cancellation-only Python 3.7 compatibility shim removed before candidate hash verification

failed_attempts.approach: Add delegation on a plausible client-side WebSocket surface.
failed_attempts.observed_result: The existing suite passed, but evaluator comparison showed that the patch targeted the wrong public surface.
failed_attempts.why_failed: The repair did not begin at WebSocketHandler.set_nodelay or follow the current server-side ownership chain.

recovery_steps: Start at the exact public method named in the issue and identify the resource it is expected to control.
Trace ownership through each abstraction until the currently active stream is found.
Add a focused contract test that calls the public wrapper and asserts delegation on the active stream.
Route the wrapper through the protocol object instead of retaining the stale direct stream reference.
Run the focused regression, related WebSocket tests, and the complete historical suite.
Keep environment-only compatibility shims outside the candidate patch and recheck the candidate hash after removing them.

verification_method.summary: The corrected regression failed before repair and passed after repair; 46 WebSocket tests passed with one skip, and the complete historical suite passed 1,146 tests with 50 skips.

agent_ready_instructions: Use this only when a public wrapper controls a resource whose ownership has moved behind another abstraction. Reproduce the failure at the named public entry point, trace the current ownership chain, and verify that the wrapper reaches the active resource. Reject a suite-green patch that targets a different surface. Add a focused delegation contract test, then run related and full regression checks. Keep environment compatibility shims separate from the repair. Abstain if the wrapper is supposed to own an independent resource.

subtasks.description: Detect a green-suite false positive by checking the real public delegation path
lessons: A proxy repair can pass the existing suite while targeting the wrong public surface; the contract test must begin at the caller named in the issue.

subtasks.description: Route WebSocketHandler set_nodelay through the protocol to the active stream
lessons: When resource ownership moves behind an abstraction, public controls must follow the ownership chain instead of retaining a stale direct reference.

constraints: CPython 3.7 was unavailable on macOS arm64; the complete suite used isolated CPython 3.8.20 with a temporary cancellation-only compatibility shim that was removed after testing.
The first frozen candidate targeted the wrong client surface and was rejected after evaluator comparison; the successful second attempt was therefore evaluator-informed.
No raw logs, prompts, source patches, credentials, or private workspace paths are published.
lessons: Trace delegation from the issue's public entry point through every ownership boundary before choosing where to add a proxy.
A full green legacy suite cannot validate behavior that has no regression test; add a focused contract test that asserts the exact delegate call.
Reject a green patch when evaluator comparison proves that it repaired a plausible but different API surface.
Keep runtime-compatibility shims separate from the candidate patch and recheck the candidate hash after removing them.
